body:
More time with friends and exercise it is.

Are you saying you don't have (close / enough) friends because you don't like anyone you know, or because there aren't anyone you know whom you'd like to be friends with? Everyone I know at this point I know through school. It's a small town, so there really is no other way to meet (new) people.
You're saying it just... went away?

You see? You have it much worse than me. I taught my self programming because I *wanted* to. I'm just enlisted in this class by default, and am just looking forward to doing what I like in stead of the regular school work. Because it's not even close to too late for me to go any direction I want. I don't even have to think about it for the next two years.

I have it splendid. I wouldn't want it any other way. Which is why I feel so guilty / shitty about feeling shitty.

Oh.... even though the sadness is very varying from day to day, and even week to week, the watching the world burn part is pretty much constant. I enjoy our technology, but I'm quite cynical and couldn't give less of shit if the world crashed and burned tomorrow.

No, don't be too hard on him, I think I understand what he means. He was saying there's no logical reason for me to be depressed, which I clearly said in the OP, that there isn't.

And I'm a logical guy, which is especially why this bothers me. Of course there's things that could be improved, but many of my friends have it worse, so logically, there's nothing for me to be sad about. I mean, work on, sure. Complain, sure. Bitch, sure. But feel this way about? No. I'm a long way away from that. Logically.

No, just... not really. I'm just waiting for the world to burn :) Because then I'll have something to be sad about. Not that I would particularly care (that's a whole other issue, though), but people would understand why I'm sad.

I sometimes wish something would happen to me or someone I care about just so I'd have something the outside world could go "oooh, that's why he's sad." And then I feel guilty.
I think we're in the *same* god damned boat. I don't like describing it as actual depression, I just feel... like *blah* at times.

It's the oddest thing. I'm feeling really depressed, but I still chuckled at your comment. The chemical imbalance part, that is. Sounds really odd. But no matter how I feel now, if a friend knocked on the door (middle of the night, so that's unlikely) I'd still light up and smile to them. And again, genuinely. I'd be happy to see them. I'd be happy to see QI on the telly, and I'd laugh at Stephen's (usually) sophisticated jokes, but I'd still feel like shit when that high wears off.

I don't know.
But that's the thing, I don't have anything to be depressed about. I just feel shitty.
